LeafBlaster Pro vs LeafFilter: A Practical Comparison

Published on December 20, 2024 | Reviewed October 29, 2026 | By CleanGutters Lighting

Which Products This Page Compares

This page compares two professionally installed stainless-steel micro-mesh gutter guards: LeafBlaster Pro by Gutterglove, the guard CleanGutters Lighting installs, and LeafFilter.

Gutterglove, Inc. makes more than one gutter guard, and the designs and warranties are not all the same. LeafBlaster Pro alone comes in three versions: Frame-Reinforced Stainless Steel Micro-Mesh, Stainless Steel Micro-Mesh and All-Aluminum. This comparison covers the two stainless-steel micro-mesh versions. It does not describe other Gutterglove products. Your written quote names the exact product for your home.

Every detail below comes from the manufacturers' own current pages, linked in each section. Where a manufacturer does not publish something, we say so rather than guess.

LeafFilter: What the Manufacturer Says

  • A patented 3-piece system made up of a stainless-steel micromesh screen, a uPVC frame and internal hidden hangers.
  • The micromesh is surgical-grade stainless steel, 275 microns fine, which LeafFilter says keeps out shingle grit.
  • The uPVC frame has a built-in pitch so the guard sheds debris while taking in water. Surface tension draws water through the mesh and into the gutter.
  • It installs directly on your existing gutters.
  • LeafFilter advertises a lifetime, transferable warranty and a no-clog guarantee. It also says it will correct installation errors that could cause clogs inside the gutter. LeafFilter's page refers you to a local representative for the full warranty text.

LeafFilter is not a reverse-curve guard and does not use a double-layer mesh. An earlier version of this page described it that way, and that was wrong. Source: LeafFilter: What is LeafFilter?

LeafBlaster Pro: What the Manufacturer Says

  • Stainless Steel Micro-Mesh: premium-grade stainless-steel mesh on T4-hardened 6063 aluminum support rails, with a patented Z-Bend shape that lifts leaves and needles off the surface so wind and rain can carry them away. Gutterglove calls this the version most homes end up with.
  • Frame-Reinforced Stainless Steel Micro-Mesh: the same mesh on a continuous T6-hardened extruded aluminum frame, built for heavy branches, snow loads and large mature trees.
  • Both versions are installed by professional contractors only.
  • Gutterglove says the mesh blocks leaves, pine needles, seeds and shingle grit, and that the stainless steel does not rust or corrode.

Source: LeafBlaster Pro: Three Gutter Guards, Compared

Written Warranty: Read the Fine Print on Both

LeafBlaster Pro limited parts warranty (version updated July 1, 2025):

  • 40 years against defects in manufactured parts. Gutterglove chooses whether to repair or replace.
  • Parts only. It does not cover labor (such as removing and reinstalling the guard), hardware or shipping.
  • Reduced to 10 years in coastal areas, which Gutterglove defines as anywhere within 5 miles of a shoreline, including oceans, gulfs, seas and lakes. That matters for South Jersey shore towns and homes near lakes.
  • Transferable to later owners. You must keep the warranty document and original receipt, and claims must be made within 90 days of discovering a defect.
  • It is void for improper installation (including contact with copper), and it excludes storm and hail damage, sap, moss, droppings, improper maintenance and damaged gutters or structures. It does not cover the contractor's installation work.

Source: LeafBlaster Pro 40-Year Limited Parts Warranty (PDF)

LeafFilter: the manufacturer's page advertises a lifetime, transferable warranty and a no-clog guarantee, and says it will correct installation errors that could cause clogs. It does not publish the full terms on that page, so ask for the complete written warranty before you sign.

Bottom line on warranties: the two are written very differently. Compare the actual documents, not the headline number. Coverage for any particular home is decided by the manufacturer under its own terms.

Installation

  • Both are professional-install products, and both mount on the gutter system rather than replacing it.
  • Gutter removal is not automatically required for either guard. If your existing gutters are sagging, leaking, loose or pitched wrong, repairs or replacement may be the right first step. That should be spelled out in your written quote, not assumed.
  • How long an install takes depends on the length of the roofline, the number of stories, access and the condition of the existing gutters, so we do not quote a standard time.
  • Whether a guard suits your gutter size, roof type and roof edge is confirmed at the inspection, not promised in advance.

Maintenance: Lower, Not Zero

Fine stainless mesh keeps most debris out of the gutter itself, but no guard should be sold as maintenance-free. Pollen, sap, moss, roof grit and wet leaves can sit on top of any fine mesh. Gutterglove's own warranty excludes sap, moss, droppings and improper maintenance. Plan on an occasional look from the ground and a light cleaning of the mesh surface when it is needed, especially under heavy tree cover.

What Affects the Price

We do not publish price ranges for either brand, because the real number depends on your home. The main factors are:

  • Roofline length: the total feet of gutter to be covered.
  • Access: the number of stories, roof pitch, landscaping and how safely ladders can be placed.
  • Existing gutter condition: whether hangers, pitch, seams or fascia need attention first.
  • Product version: standard or frame-reinforced micro-mesh, chosen based on trees and weather exposure.

Whichever company you talk to, ask for a written quote that names the exact product, lists any gutter repairs and includes a copy of the manufacturer's warranty. For more on what we check, see our gutter guards page and gutter services overview.

How to Choose

  • Construction: aluminum rails or frame with a Z-Bend mesh (LeafBlaster Pro), or a uPVC frame with internal hangers (LeafFilter).
  • Warranty structure: a published 40-year parts-only warranty with a coastal reduction, or an advertised lifetime warranty. Read both in full.
  • Your home: the trees overhead, how close you are to the shore or a lake, and the condition of your current gutters.
  • The installer: who actually does the work, who you call if something goes wrong, and what is in writing.
